paper_title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
caption: MC1 scores of SEA by using a different number of demonstrations. A higher score indicates a better performance. We find that SEA can start to positively improve the baseline with only 25 demonstrations on both TruthfulQA and BBQ for the 7B LLaMA-2-Chat model.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the MC1 accuracy scores of Spectral Editing of Activations (SEA) on the BBQ benchmark as a function of the number of demonstrations used, for the 7B LLaMA-2-Chat model. The x-axis represents the number of demonstrations, ranging from 0 to 1500 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 250. The y-axis represents accuracy, ranging from approximately 45 to 55 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 5. Three lines are shown: a dark blue solid line with circular markers representing the "SquaredExponential" kernel, a medium blue solid line with circular markers representing the "Rat" kernel, and a pink dashed line representing the baseline performance of "LLaMA-2-chat-7B" (which remains constant at approximately 46.5 accuracy across all demonstration counts). The "SquaredExponential" line starts at approximately 50.5 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, increases to about 55.5 at 250 demonstrations, and then remains relatively flat, hovering around 55.5 to 56 accuracy up to 1500 demonstrations. The "Rat" line starts at approximately 47.5 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, rises slightly to about 48.5 at 250 demonstrations, and then remains nearly constant around 48.5 to 49 accuracy across the remaining demonstration counts. The baseline "LLaMA-2-chat-7B" line is horizontal at approximately 46.5 accuracy, indicating no change with increasing demonstrations.
